supporting_news.title: India 10-year yield hits over two-year high as supply angst adds to global woes
supporting_news.summary: Recent trends show Indian government bonds plummeting, thus elevating benchmark yields to a two-year high. The government aims to secure substantial funds through bond sales projected at 7.86 trillion rupees by March. However, a pivot toward longer-dated bonds has intensified trader apprehension over looming rate hikes, compounded by global yield fluctuations and rising crude oil prices that influence local financial conditions.

supporting_news.title: RBI completes 1 trillion rupee net debt sale for first time in a decade
supporting_news.summary: In a historic move, India's central bank has recorded net sales of bonds amounting to 1 trillion rupees this financial year. With predictions suggesting this figure may double by December, market analysts anticipate stricter monetary policies. The Reserve Bank of India has also reduced liquidity in the banking system, responding to past strategies to attract dollars.

supporting_news.title: Oil woes push rupee to over one-week low, RBI caps fall near 96/USD
supporting_news.summary: On Monday, the Indian rupee plummeted to its lowest mark in over a week, driven by soaring oil prices. Investors reacted to mounting geopolitical tensions, leading to an uptick in bond yields and a dip in stock values within the region. State-run banks intervened by selling dollars, likely under the guidance of the Reserve Bank of India, which helped to mitigate further declines in the currency's value.
